name: Sanghare Margin Analytics for WooCommerce
author: sadiosan23

sections.description:
Sanghare Margin Analytics for WooCommerce provides a fully functional local profitability analytics workflow for WooCommerce stores.

Core capabilities:

  • Historical COGS snapshots so past margin calculations remain reproducible when product costs change.
  • Net revenue, COGS, gross profit and gross margin analytics.
  • Order-level and product-level profitability views.
  • Refund-aware calculations.
  • Profit Data Quality scoring focused on COGS coverage and reliability.
  • Background backfills and recalculation audit history.
  • HPOS-safe WooCommerce order APIs.
  • Dedicated plugin tables for analytics data.

All analytics calculations in this WordPress.org package run locally on the site, and every included feature is available immediately after activation.

Privacy

Sanghare Margin Analytics for WooCommerce processes WooCommerce profitability analytics locally in the WordPress database. The WordPress.org edition does not require a license service and does not intentionally transmit order-level revenue, COGS, margin or customer-order analytics to an external service.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce 10.3 or newer.
  2. Upload or install Sanghare Margin Analytics for WooCommerce.
  3. Activate the plugin.
  4. Open WooCommerce > Margin Analytics.
  5. Build the initial analytics dataset when prompted.
  6. Review Data Quality before relying on historical profitability reports.
sections.faq:
Does the plugin modify historical product costs?

No. Historical cost snapshots are stored separately so previously calculated orders remain reproducible.

Is HPOS supported?

Yes. The plugin uses WooCommerce order APIs and declares HPOS compatibility.

Does the plugin send store analytics to an external service?

No. This WordPress.org package performs its profitability calculations locally and does not require a remote analytics or licensing service.

What is the Profit Data Quality Score?

It measures the coverage and reliability of the cost data used for gross-profit analytics. It does not grade the financial performance of the store.
